chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman whom a man married, and the woman gave him the dower and stipulated upon him that copulation and divorce would be in her hand. He (peace be upon him) said: He opposed the Sunnah and assigned the right to one who is not its rightful owner, and the judgement is that upon the man is the dower, and that copulation and divorce are in his hand, and that is the Sunnah.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wife stipulates in the marriage contract that she holds the right to divorce and consummation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that the wife’s stipulation of exclusive control over consummation and divorce is 'contrary to the Sunnah' because it transfers rights to one who is not their natural holder, thereby disrupting the customary marital structure. While the husband remains liable for the full dower, the default authority (Sunnah) of the husband in these matters is upheld, illustrating the Shia principle that stipulations must align with the inherent nature of the contract rather than arbitrarily reversing established roles.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, form Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a woman who got married to a man, so the woman kept a dower and stipulated upon him that the copulation and the divorce would be in her hands’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be opposing the Sunnah and he has placed the right upon the one who is not rightful for it, and the judgement is that upon the man is the dower, and that in his hand would be the copulation and the divorce, and that is the Sunnah’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “About the case of a woman who marries a man and she as part of her mahr (dower) says that going to bed will be in her control as well as divorce, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is against the Sunnah and has entrusted the right with one who is not the right person for it. Judgment requires that the man must pay mahr (dower). He has the right to go to bed and divorce and that is the Sunnah.’”
